title: International tourism has recovered at scale, but mobility, spending, regional dependence, and cultural exchange remain uneven
source_unit: UN Tourism, International Tourism Highlights 2025 Edition and World Tourism Barometer updates
geography: Global international tourism with regional and destination comparisons; 2024 annual results and 2025-2026 updates

denominator.unit: global international tourist arrivals and tourism economy

international_arrivals_2024.unit: millions of international tourist arrivals in 2024

pandemic_recovery.value: 2024 marked the recovery of international tourism from the sector's worst crisis

visitor_spending.value: visitor spending continued to grow strongly alongside the recovery in arrivals

observations.method: UN Tourism compilation of international arrival, tourism-receipt, and country statistical data collected from destinations and international organizations.
observations.uncertainty: Arrivals are trips rather than unique people and do not measure resident burden, visitor welfare, job quality, environmental pressure, or local value retention; recovery varies by destination and purpose.
observations.subgroup: International visitors, destination residents, tourism workers and firms, transport systems, cultural sites, and tourism-dependent economies.
observations.counterinterpretation: Tourism recovery can support livelihoods, cultural exchange, and public revenue while concentrating benefits, increasing housing and infrastructure pressure, and exposing destinations to shocks.

denominator.unit: international tourism receipts and tourism services exports

international_tourism_receipts_2024.unit: billion US dollars in international tourism receipts in 2024, in real terms as reported by UN Tourism

q1_2025_arrival_growth.unit: percent growth in international tourist arrivals in the first quarter of 2025 compared with Q1 2024

q1_2025_air_demand_growth.unit: percent increase in international air-transport demand in Q1 2025 compared with Q1 2024

observations.method: UN Tourism World Tourism Barometer synthesis of international arrivals, tourism receipts, and aviation-demand indicators.
observations.uncertainty: Receipts are affected by exchange rates, inflation, trip length, and accounting conventions; air demand and arrival growth are related but not equivalent measures of tourism activity.
observations.subgroup: Tourists, airlines, accommodation and hospitality firms, destination governments, cultural industries, and service-export economies.
observations.counterinterpretation: Faster spending growth than arrivals may reflect prices, longer stays, or higher-value segments rather than broader access or more equitable tourism income.

observations.period: 2025-2026; changing travel flows and short-term mobility

denominator.unit: UN Tourism global and regional tourism monitoring frame

q1_2026_arrivals.unit: millions of international tourists traveling in the first quarter of 2026

q1_2026_year_on_year_change.unit: million more international tourists in Q1 2026 than in Q1 2025

travel_shock_channels.value: air connectivity, geopolitical tensions, prices, safety conditions, and destination capacity shape uneven travel flows

observations.method: UN Tourism World Tourism Barometer current monitoring of international arrivals and short-term travel conditions.
observations.uncertainty: Quarterly figures are provisional and seasonal; changes in routes, conflicts, prices, and reporting coverage can alter comparisons and do not identify individual travel motives.
observations.subgroup: Travelers, destinations, airlines, tourism workers, border and visa systems, and regions exposed to geopolitical or infrastructure shocks.
observations.counterinterpretation: Resilient aggregate demand can mask destination-level collapse, substitution toward safer routes, or unequal access caused by prices and visa barriers.

observations.period: 2024-2026; tourism as cultural and place-based economy

denominator.unit: UN Tourism publication and destination-development framework

tourism_scope.value: tourism connects mobility, cultural exchange, service work, destination infrastructure, and regional development

regional_dependence.value: tourism receipts and arrivals are unevenly distributed across destinations and regions

resilience_question.value: recovery depends on connectivity, diversification, safety, public policy, and the capacity to retain local benefits

observations.method: UN Tourism synthesis of destination statistics, regional performance, tourism exports, outbound travel, and policy context.
observations.uncertainty: The publication describes sector-level patterns rather than measuring cultural meaning, resident consent, or distribution of tourism income in individual places.
observations.subgroup: Visitors, residents, cultural organizations, small businesses, workers, public authorities, and communities in tourism-dependent places.
observations.counterinterpretation: Tourism can strengthen local cultural economies and mutual understanding, but commodification, overcrowding, displacement, and external ownership can weaken local agency.

related_sources.claim: OECD Tourism Trends and Policies 2026 provides complementary destination, host-community, and resilience analysis.
World Bank Tourism Watch provides complementary geopolitical and uneven-recovery monitoring.

boundary: This record adds a global tourism demand, mobility, cultural-exchange, and place-based consumption route. It uses aggregate arrival, revenue, and sector-level publication evidence, not individual travel motives, resident sentiment, worker quality, local housing effects, or causal tourism-policy estimates.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: Official UN Tourism International Tourism Highlights and World Tourism Barometer materials were reviewed for the 2024 global recovery, receipts, 2025 and 2026 arrival updates, aviation demand, and tourism-as-cultural/place economy claims.
